messages.author: 707ae3d6583b1b8d
messages.subject: fit plm changes in the vignettes
parts:
Dear Henrik,

there is a change in the fitting method between the latest and former
vignette for SNP5&6.

# old vignette style
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

# new vignette style
if (length(findUnitsTodo(plm)) > 0) {
# Fit CN probes quickly (~5-10s/array + some overhead)
units <- fitCnProbes(plm, verbose=verbose)
str(units)
# Fit remaining units, i.e. SNPs (~5-10min/array)
units <- fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
str(units)
}

This is just about computational speed, so you have to expect the same
result with both methods?

What does really "fitCnProbes" do compared to "fit"?

Best Regards
Marco

messages.author: a5f6afcbe5b17914
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] fit plm changes in the vignettes
parts:
Hi,

fitCnProbes() and fit() give identical results for CN units that
consist of single CN probes. More details on Page 'Improving
processing time':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/improving-processing-time

This is also explained in the Vignette 'Estimation of total copy
numbers using the CRMA v2 method (10K-6.0) ':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/estimation-of-total-copy-numbers-using-the-crma-v2-method

which you should be using since it uses CRMAv2 for estimating CNs and
CRMAv2 has been shown (published) to perform really well.

The Vignette 'Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)' is not using
CRMAv2 [I cannot update this vignette with such a comment for the
reasons explained on the front page of the group; we will very soon
move to a new site though].

/Henrik

PS. Your definition of "new" is "old", the vignette I think you are
using was updated to use fitCnProbes() nearly 12 months ago.
